Tests network security basics and practical CI tooling for a multi-tenant cluster. It reinforces a concrete, replicable gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end controls around data contracts, provenance, and policy enforcement in a multi-tenant data platform. Candidates must describe concrete artifacts, tools, and integration points, not abstractions.

## Key Concepts
- Data contracts and central registry validation
- Software bill of materials (SBOM) generation
- Reproducible build digest tying code, contract, and dependencies
- Artifact signing and attestations
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/contract-ci.yml
name: Contract CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate contract
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run validate-contract -- --registry https://registry.example.com
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          npm ci && npm run generate-sbom
      - name: Compute digest
        run: |
          echo -n "$(git rev-parse --verify HEAD)" > digest.txt
          shasum -a 256 contract.json sbom.json >> digest.txt
      - name: Attest
        run: |
          echo "attestation" && cat digest.txt
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll out this gate to multiple cloud regions with differing registry endpoints?
- How would you test failure modes (invalid contract, missing SBOM, digest mismatch) in CI and in runtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a scalable, automated policy gate across multi-cloud clusters using Gatekeeper/OPA, Cosign attestations, and runtime security constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Cosign attestation and image provenance
- Registry allowlist and image provenance checks
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop capabilities
- CI integration and gatekeeper audit verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (Gatekeeper) minimal sketch
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8ssecuredcontainers
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecuredContainers
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8ssecuredcontainers
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not signed(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Container image %v must be cosign-signed", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not allowed_registry(container.image)
          msg := sprintf("Registry %v not in allowlist", [container.image])
        }
        
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
          not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
          msg := "Container must run as non-root"
        }
```

- Demonstrates understanding of OPA/Gatekeeper policy structure
- Shows proper cosign attestation validation approach
- Includes comprehensive runtime security constraints
- Outlines practical CI/CD integration strategy

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of Kubernetes manifests is a practical, repeatable gate in real projects. This tests understanding of policy-as-code, tooling choices (Kyverno vs Gatekeeper), constraint design for host access controls and image source controls, and CI integration in GitHub Actions with ephemeral test clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper
- Constraints for host access (hostNetwork, hostPath, hostPort, privileged containers)
- Image source controls (allowed registries) and imagePullPolicy enforcement
- CI integration in GitHub Actions using KinD or similar ephemeral clusters

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-host-access
spec:
  rules:
  - name: block-host-network
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork is not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
  - name: block-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not allowed"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ contains(element.volumes[].hostPath, '') }}"
          operator: "NotEqual"
          value: ""
```

## Minimal Policy (Combined)
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: security-guardrails
spec:
  rules:
  - name: deny-host-network-port
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork and hostPort are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: "false"
          hostPort: "0"
  - name: deny-host-path
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "hostPath volumes are not permitted"
      deny:
        conditions:
        - key: "{{ @ }}"
          operator: "AnyNotIn"
          value: [""]
      foreach:
        - list: "spec.volumes[?hostPath]"
          deny: true
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Privileged containers are not permitted"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              privileged: "false"
  - name: allowed-registries
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Images must come from approved registries"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "registry.company.com/*"
            imagePullPolicy: "Always"
```

## Failing Manifest (hostPath + hostNetwork)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: docker.io/myapp:latest
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    volumeMounts:
    - name: host-volume
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: host-volume
    hostPath:
      path: /etc
```

## Passing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.company.com/myapp:v1.0
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Validation
```bash
# Install Kyverno locally
brew install kyverno

# Apply policies
kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml

# Validate a manifest
kyverno validate insecure-pod.yaml
```

## CI Validation (GitHub Actions)
```yaml
name: Validate Manifests
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Create KinD cluster
      run: kind create cluster
    - name: Install Kyverno
      run: |
        kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
        kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kyverno -n kyverno --timeout=120s
    - name: Apply policies
      run: kubectl apply -f security-guardrails.yaml
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f insecure-pod.yaml || echo "Expected failure"
        kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f secure-pod.yaml
```

            spec:

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement real-world security gates that combine image scanning, attestation, and policy enforcement in a scalable multi‑tenant environment.

- Admission control with OPA/Kyverno
- SBOMs and CVE scoring via Trivy
- Image signing with cosign and Rekor attestation
- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
# OPA policy (partial) enforcing CVE threshold and SBOM signing
package gate
default allow = false
allow {
  input.images[_].cve_score <= 6.0
  input.images[_].sbom_signed
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
- Evaluates practical policy design for observability in cloud-native platforms
- Tests knowledge of admission control, Kyverno policies, and CI integration

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation methods (sidecars vs. environment variables)
- Kyverno policy patterns and validation rules
- CI verification of policy enforcement and runtime tracing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-otel-tracing
spec:
 rules:
 - name: require-otel-annotation
   match:
     resources:
       kinds: [Deployment]
   validate:
     message: "Deployment must have otel.instrumentation=enabled annotation"
     anyPattern:
     - metadata:
         annotations:
           otel.instrumentation: "enabled"
 - name: require-otel-configuration
   match:
     resources:
       kinds: [Deployment]
   validate:
     message: "Deployment must configure tracing via otel-collector sidecar or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"
     anyPattern:
     - spec:
         template:
           spec:
             containers:
             - name: "otel-collector"
     - spec:
         template:
           spec:
             containers:
             - env:
               - name: "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"
```

## CI Test Plan
1. Deploy policy to test cluster
2. Test compliance scenarios (valid deployments)
3. Test rejection scenarios (missing annotation, no tracing config)
4. Verify policy enforces during deployment
5. Validate tracing functionality in approved deployments
